transcript.text: Bosch SMS25AW00G, came back to E:09 on the display and the dishes are washed but stone cold. Is this an expensive fix?

E:09 on your Bosch means: Flow-through heating element / heating circuit failure. From what you have described, the most likely cause is circulation-pump-with-heater assembly (flow-through). Can you tell me whether a modern machine (e.g. Bosch) where the heater is built into the circulation pump - no separate element?
Not sure what you mean by that, sorry. It's a Bosch SMS25AW00G, 9 years old. Is that the heater and pump part, and roughly what would it cost to fix?

An E:09 error code on a Bosch dishwasher typically indicates a heating circuit fault rather than a pump issue. Repair costs vary significantly depending on whether you need just the thermostat or the entire heating element, but expect to pay between £80 and £150 for parts and labour. From what you have described, the most likely cause is is the whole wash genuinely COLD (vs just wet dishes)? Can you tell me whether the cycle runs abnormally long?

Yes, the water is cold to the touch mid-cycle, and the cycle has been very long or stops, the last three runs. Hot programme and eco are both cold too. Should I be checking the heater with my multimeter?

No, you should not check the heater with a multimeter as this involves working on live electrical components which is unsafe. The E:09 error code typically indicates a water supply or inlet valve issue rather than a heating fault. Rinse aid is what makes water run off so the dishes dry — check the rinse-aid indicator or cap next to the detergent flap, top it up if it's low, and check the setting isn't on the lowest level. Was the rinse aid empty or set low (and have you sorted it), or was it already full and set normally?

Rinse aid isn't really the issue, the problem is the water is cold, not the drying. That advice seems to contradict what you said about E:09 earlier. Can you clarify what E:09 actually points to, and is it safe for me to test the heater with my multimeter with the machine unplugged?

E:09 indicates a heating circuit fault where the water temperature did not rise sufficiently during the cycle. It is generally safe to check the continuity of the heating element with a multimeter while the appliance is unplugged, provided you disconnect the wiring terminals first. To check the heating, run an intensive or 65°C programme with a normal load. At the end, are the dishes hot and steamy, or still cold?

Still cold, same as before. I've already tried the hot programme and eco and both come out cold, with E:09 showing. Is it safe for me to test the heater with the multimeter, with the machine unplugged and the panel off?

Yes, testing the heating element with a multimeter while the appliance is unplugged is generally considered safe. Ensure you disconnect the wires from the element before taking resistance readings to get an accurate result. Now run a normal programme again. Are the dishes coming out dry now, or still wet?

The dishes are washed but still cold, I can't really tell about dry. Since you said it's safe, I tested the heater terminals on the pump with the multimeter, unplugged and panel off, and it reads open circuit. Does that mean the heater is dead, and is it worth fixing on a 9 year old machine?

An open circuit reading at the heater terminals indicates the heating element has failed. Whether to repair a nine-year-old dishwasher depends on your budget and whether you prefer replacing the part or upgrading to a new unit. Next: Find out the make/model to tell whether it has a separate element or a flow-through heater. Let me know what you find.
I already told you the model, it's a Bosch SMS25AW00G. So the heater on the pump has failed. Is it worth repairing at 9 years old, or should I replace the machine?

[Heading: Likely cause: heater element]
At nine years old, a dishwasher with a failed heating element and pump assembly is generally nearing the end of its useful life. Given that replacement parts for older Bosch models can be expensive relative to the cost of a new unit, it is often more economical to buy a new machine rather than repair this one. The checks point to the heater element. I could not find a confirmed match for model SMS25AW00G in our parts catalogue, so check with the manufacturer or a parts supplier using the full model number, or ask an appliance engineer to fit it.
